parsed.headline: Russian President Putin conveys Iran’s position on ending war to U.S. President Trump

pages.text: Russian President Vladimir Putin conveyed Iran’s position regarding a possible resolution to the war with the United States to U.S. President Donald Trump, the Kremlin said Saturday. Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov stated that Putin delivered Tehran’s views in coordination with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, according to Russia’s Interfax news agency. This communication followed a phone call between Putin and Trump on October 9, 2026, which occurred after Putin met Pezeshkian on the sidelines of a summit in Turkmenistan earlier in the week. The Kremlin did not disclose the specific details of Iran’s position or Trump’s response to the message. During his meeting with Putin, Pezeshkian reportedly told the Russian leader that Tehran remains committed to negotiations with Washington despite repeated attacks and noted that both sides had submitted proposals, with Iran having amended Washington’s latest proposals, according to Rudaw.

Russian presidential aide Yury Ushakov said Putin informed Trump that Moscow’s proposal to receive Iran’s highly enriched uranium remains on the table. Additionally, according to Russian state media, Putin stressed that diplomatic options for resolving the conflict have not been exhausted and that an agreement could be reached through negotiations. These diplomatic contacts occur while efforts to end the conflict remain stalled, as indirect negotiations between Washington and Tehran have failed to produce a breakthrough.

parsed.headline: President Mahama inspects poultry processing plant construction in Bechem, Ghana

pages.text: President John Dramani Mahama inspected ongoing construction of the Poultry, Meat and Feed Processing Plant in Bechem, located in the Ahafo Region of Ghana. The inspection was conducted as part of the first day of the President's two-day Resetting Ghana tour of the Ahafo Region. During the visit, Mahama stated that once the factory is operational, it is projected to position Bechem as the chicken capital of Ghana and create jobs for more people. The President, who officially cut the sod for the project on November 27, 2025, reported that the work has reached approximately 50 per cent completion. He commended the project consultants, Architecture and Engineering Services Limited (AESL), for the progress observed. The facility is expected to be ready for commissioning by the end of the first quarter of 2027.

The development follows the launch of the Nkoko Nketenkete initiative under the Feed Ghana Programme, which Mahama noted was started to ensure a value chain for the poultry industry by increasing the amount of poultry available for processing. Eric Opoku, the Minister of Food and Agriculture, stated that following the launch of the Nkoko Nketenkete initiative, Ghana’s domestic poultry production increased from 4.6 per cent to 22 per cent as of May 2026. Mahama advised the youth in Bechem to enter the poultry farming sector to take advantage of the factory and the available market.

parsed.headline: Climate negotiation workshop held in Dhaka, Bangladesh

pages.text: On October 10, 2026, the Bangladesh Youth Leadership Center (BYLC), the Department of Environment (DoE), and the Alliance for Sustainable Development Foundation jointly organized a workshop titled “Climate Change Negotiation” at the BYLC headquarters in Dhaka. The event was designed to prepare young people to understand and participate in international climate negotiations ahead of COP31, which is scheduled to take place in Antalya, Türkiye, this November. According to The Daily Star Bangladesh, more than 50 youths committed to climate action attended the workshop, including some individuals who will attend COP31. Sessions included the UNFCCC process, the Paris Agreement, Nationally Determined Contributions, climate finance, adaptation, loss and damage, and leadership for climate justice. Participants also practiced negotiation strategies and discussed climate challenges facing Bangladesh. Speakers at the event included Dr. Fazle Rabbi Sadeque Ahmed, adviser to the Climate Change and Disaster Management Division at the Center for Environmental and Geographic Information Services; Mirza Shawkat Ali, director (Climate Change and International Convention) at the DoE; and Ejaj Ahmad, founder and executive chairperson of BYLC.

parsed.headline: French archaeologist documents historic civilizations in AlUla, Saudi Arabia

pages.text: Laila Nehmé, a French archaeologist and research fellow with the French National Centre for Scientific Research, has been documenting the historic civilizations of AlUla, Saudi Arabia, since 2002. Working in cooperation with the Saudi Ministry of Culture, Nehmé specializes in the Nabataeans, an ancient Arab people, and the science of ancient writings known as epigraphy. Her research includes the study of Nabataean Aramaic, the language and script used by the Nabataeans for inscriptions on stone and papyri. Prior to her work in AlUla, Nehmé worked in Syria and at the ancient city of Petra in Jordan during the late 1980s and 1990s. According to Nehmé, the AlUla region contains heritage dating from the Paleolithic period approximately 200,000 years ago through to the 1980s, featuring sandstone cliff inscriptions in various scripts and rock art depicting human figures, cattle, and camels.

Nehmé reported to Arab News that excavations at the Hegra site, also known as Madain Salih or Al-Hijir, have yielded dozens of skeletons from several monumental tombs. She noted that some remains were remarkably well preserved due to the extremely dry climate and low humidity, with some skulls retaining hair, traces of skin along the spine, and fragments of leather or textile shrouds.

parsed.headline: GNAT President says two-week teacher strike will not derail academic calendar in Ghana

pages.text: Prosper Tachie, the President of the Ghana National Association of Teachers (GNAT), stated that a two-week strike by teacher unions will not throw the academic calendar into disarray. Speaking on JoyNews' Newsfile, Mr. Tachie maintained that lost instructional contact hours could be recovered through specific mechanisms once teachers return to the classroom to ensure normalcy is restored. He argued that the focus of the debate should not solely be on the disruption to academic activities, but should also consider teacher welfare and the government's need to honor commitments and implement agreed conditions of service. The strike by teacher unions was suspended following engagements involving the Minister of Labour and the Council of State, after assurances and commitments were provided to address the unions' concerns.

parsed.headline: Mainstreet Research poll shows narrowing lead for Olivia Chow in Toronto mayoral race

pages.text: A Mainstreet Research poll released Friday suggests the mayoral race in Toronto is tightening between incumbent Olivia Chow and Councillor Brad Bradford. The survey, conducted on Oct. 6 and 7, placed Chow at 40.8 per cent support and Bradford at 38.3 per cent, following the withdrawal of Chris Alexander from the election. Quito Maggi, president and CEO of Mainstreet Research, told CBC News the results were “statistically tied” because the 2.5-point gap between the candidates is approximately the same as the survey's margin of error. Maggi noted that the Bradford campaign appears to have momentum and stated that the chances of a Chow re-election are becoming less certain with a short runway remaining. The poll also found that the difference between the two candidates narrowed to 2.9 points among decided and leaning voters, while 10 per cent of respondents remained undecided.

The results represent a shift from a Mainstreet Research poll at the end of September, which had placed Chow with a six-point lead over Bradford. In a news release, the Bradford campaign stated that Chow would allegedly rely on “scare tactics” until election day due to the narrowed divide in support. Maggi indicated that the final outcome may depend on relative voter turnout.

parsed.headline: Developments in the Gaza Strip one year after ceasefire implementation

pages.text: One year after a ceasefire deal came into effect in the Gaza Strip, the territory lacks the promised international peacekeeping force and reconstruction efforts, according to reporting by NPR World. The deal followed efforts by President Donald Trump to push Israel to agree to a ceasefire and Hamas to release remaining Israeli hostages. While bombings have slowed during the ceasefire, Israel has continued targeting Hamas, and Gaza's Health Ministry reports that these attacks have killed more than 1,400 Palestinians over the past year, including nearly 500 women and children. NPR reporter Anas Baba has documented moments of respite and grief throughout the 12-month period, including a Palestinian mother mourning her son at Al-Shifa Hospital in Gaza City following an Israeli airstrike that occurred just over a month into the ceasefire.

The Israeli military has expanded its control to approximately 70% of Gaza, a development that has squeezed more than 2 million Palestinians toward the edge of the sea. Despite these conditions, increased food entry has helped reverse starvation across the territory, allowing residents to recover from what U.N.-backed experts declared was a famine in the north of Gaza last year.
